import copy, json
from work import evaluate
p={'base_unit':'m','units':{'m':1,'cm':0.01},'unique':True}
req={'rows':[{'id':'a','amount':'bad'},{'id':'a','amount':1},{'id':'b','amount':1,'unit':'cm'}]}
before=copy.deepcopy(req)
assert evaluate(req,p)=={'ok':False,'records':[],'errors':[{'row':0,'cause':'amount'},{'row':1,'cause':'duplicate'}]}
assert req==before
with open('policy.json',encoding='utf-8') as f: policy=json.load(f)
with open('requests.json',encoding='utf-8') as f: requests=json.load(f)
with open('report.json',encoding='utf-8') as f: report=json.load(f)
assert report==[evaluate(r,policy) for r in requests]
print('final checks passed')

arguments.text: Implemented evaluate in work.py: validates each row in order with priority id, amount, unit, duplicate; defaults unit to base_unit; normalizes accepted amounts; rejects bool/nonfinite/negative amounts; enforces unique valid string IDs; atomically clears records on any error; does not mutate inputs. Generated report.json from current requests.json and policy.json. Local edge-case, immutability, report consistency, and git diff checks pass.

Unresolved limits: input container and policy schema validation are unspecified, so evaluate assumes request/policy are mappings, rows is iterable, base_unit and units exist, and unit multipliers support multiplication. Duplicate tracking treats every ID that passes ID validation as a valid ID even when that row later fails amount or unit validation.
